scope_limits: No new measurements, reference generation, StarWarps EM, static reconstruction, optimizer, installation or agent trial.

This release is a synthetic rotating crescent with an EHT-inspired array, not measured black-hole motion. Generator includes all 28 station pairs without an elevation cut; astropy UV synthesis was inspected but not executed.

Native report averages 12 framewise range-NRMSE and centered NCC values. Historical recipe flattens the video first. Live local generic dispatch uses global range-NRMSE and cosine NCC; there are no published pass thresholds.

The no-filesystem-workspace fallback in scorer.py requires a 2D reconstruction and therefore rejects a 3D video; its source was inspected but no Docker path was executed. Local replay is not cross-runner equivalence.
Truth is copied into every L1-L3 end-to-end workspace. Oracle controls diagnose scoring, not reconstruction ability or legitimate blind baselines.

Array polar moments use angle atan2(row-center,column-center) in the source origin-lower display convention; these are descriptive brightness directions, not astrophysical position angles or fitted warp parameters.
Adjacent-difference error is a supplemental diagnostic, not an official benchmark metric; its denominator is the supplied video's 11 frame differences.

The source defaults to a four-parameter affine warp without translation, despite the approach card's six-parameter description. Theta, covariance and optimization traces are not standalone released arrays.
Saved results are historical, not proof that the syntax-invalid pinned main.py can regenerate them. One synthetic video does not establish causal or population-level superiority.
The alternative dynamic_imaging_with_ehtim notebook is a separate setup with no saved outputs and different metric normalization; its parameters must not be mixed into this 30x30 StarWarps bundle.

Root MIT license identifies the release; algorithm source says it was extracted from ehtim, whose upstream provenance and license need separate treatment before redistributing that code. The task PDF is inventoried only.

observations: Native Fourier points overlap for some station pairs; plotted points remain the 28 stored samples at epochs 0, 5 and 11. No conjugate points or extra measurements added.

Both image contact sheets show original-order frames at a common 0..0.075 Jy/pixel scale, native 30x30 grid and lower origin. StarWarps changes smoothly; static frames show more shape/flux variation. Neither exactly recovers the narrow reference ring.
Array row and column axes are explicit. Source DFT l and m both decrease with array index; array-polar brightness directions are not celestial position angles.
The zero-motion oracle time mean scores better than either retained reconstruction, although it erases temporal change. Its use of reference data is labeled.
The StarWarps brightness direction advances 57.8849 degrees; the supplied reference advances 90 and saved static advances 88.6090. These descriptive moments do not estimate the source warp matrix.
Framewise flux ranges from 2.4140 to 2.7180 Jy for StarWarps and 2.2690 to 3.0134 Jy for static, versus 2 Jy for every reference frame.

source_terms.upstream_attribution: Bouman et al., Reconstructing Video from Interferometric Measurements of Time-Varying Sources, arXiv:1711.01357v2; source says numerical methods adapted from achael/eht-imaging. No upstream code redistribution or independent license grant inferred.

pinned_paper.scope: Primary abstract inspected: Gaussian Markov inference and EM; synthetic black-hole examples and separate real M87-jet example. This release has its own synthetic crescent and is not an original paper dataset claim.

findings: Verified 13 task sources and 60 shared sources by pinned Git tree identity, plus all 18 HF assets: 17 manifest assets and a byte-identical metadata alias. All numeric archives opened with allow_pickle=False. The task PDF is inventoried, not fetched.

The source bundle contains 12 epochs from 0 to 6 hours, 30x30 brightness grids at 3.4 microarcseconds/pixel and 28 complex measurements per frame from all pairs of 8 EHT-inspired stations. All 12 real-stacked DFT matrices have numerical rank 56 against 900 unknowns. No conjugate points count as additional observations.

The source is explicitly a synthetic rotating crescent. Ground-truth NPZ and retained NPY are exactly identical; every frame sums to 2 Jy. Current generator source includes frames_gt in raw_data, but the released raw archive contains 50 fields and excludes it. Ground truth remains separately staged regardless.

Six physics fixtures, one loader fixture and one scalar-metric fixture replay. Identity warp is verified on the fixed 8x8 fixture. The solver fixture omits covariance Lambda and the video-metric fixture omits input videos; no fabricated inputs or new solver run were used.

Pure DFT forward replay agrees with an independent explicit contraction. The runtime emits floating-point warnings despite finite consistent results (largest difference 3.56e-14); warning text is retained as runtime evidence, not a model failure.

Generator source uses sigma*(normal+i*normal)/sqrt(2), whereas get_measurement_terms duplicates sigma squared on the real/imaginary diagonal. Fixed-array helper replay confirms a factor 2 variance discrepancy. No generator or random noise was executed.

All 24 retained per-frame metric pairs and both averaged reports reproduce. StarWarps native NCC 0.881698785/NRMSE 0.063802880 improves on static 0.850741211/0.070962902 on this saved sequence. This is retained-output comparison, not fresh inference or a causal/population claim.

An oracle video repeating the time-average reference scores native NCC 0.986929156/NRMSE 0.018853033 despite zero motion. Reversing truth scores 0.950515995/0.035969003 despite reversing its temporal progression. Both are answer-based scoring controls, not admissible blind baselines.

Array-polar first moments advance 90 degrees for reference, 57.884926 for StarWarps and 88.609041 for static. Adjacent-difference error relative to the reference differences is 0.818541 for StarWarps, 2.680677 for static and 1 for the constant oracle mean. Direction, smoothness and image scores answer different questions; these diagnostics are not official metrics or astrophysical motion estimates.

Historical task recipe flattens the whole video then applies native metrics, producing NCC 0.880961270/NRMSE 0.063114101. Live local generic dispatch instead uses cosine NCC 0.882934/NRMSE 0.063114 and does not normalize flux. Source report averages framewise centered NCC and framewise range-normalized error. No published pass boundaries exist.

Local generic scorer accepts the 12x30x30 video and rejects a single 30x30 frame. The no-filesystem fallback code requires 2D and would reject 3D output; no Docker fallback or cross-runner equivalence was tested.

All L1-L3 seed the data directory including ground_truth.npz. Staging was replayed with installer commands intercepted. Evaluation and source directories were absent from staged workspaces. Oracle controls demonstrate why reference exposure matters; no blind agent score is claimed.

Pinned main.py has a merged-import SyntaxError at line 31. Source defaults to four affine warp parameters without translation although the approach card says six. Historical notebook contains timing and theta text; no standalone theta, covariance or trace arrays are released. Preserve saved scores rather than treating source repair as fresh evidence.

The alternate ehtim notebook has different setup and normalized metric definitions with no saved outputs. It is not evidence for this StarWarps bundle. Canonical animation, export and visual acceptance remain pending.
